programme.title: Ontological arguments: collapse atlas
programme.goal: Map, with machine-checked proofs and countermodels, which combinations of axioms, base logic and quantifier regime make Gödel-style ontological arguments consistent, yield necessary existence, force modal collapse or monotheism, and which axiom subsets are minimal for each; starting from the Lean port of Benzmüller and Scott's Notes (arXiv 2609.26806) in library/. Prior art and ground rules are in direction.md.

targets.statement: For each of the 35 examples in library/Notes closed `by countermodel`, a theorem that some structure (worlds, entities, accessibility, actuality, positivity) satisfies that variant's axioms and frame conditions while the statement fails, with every postulate discharged into hypotheses as in library/palomar, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] only; finite witnesses by `decide` where possible. Items needing an infinite countermodel are named and attempted last.

The collapse atlas: over the axiom menu (Gödel A1–A5 in binary and full-conjunction forms, Ax1Gen variants, rigidity A4, principal filter F1, ultrafilter U1, essence definitions, Fitting's extensional positivity), base logics K/KB/S4/S5 and actualist/possibilist/mixed quantifiers, decide consistency, necessary existence, modal collapse, monotheism and the ultrafilter property for every combination; then prove for each consequence the minimal axiom subsets that yield it (countermodels for every proper subset), and settle whether the ways out of collapse (dropping principality vs dropping rigidity) are distinct (Benzmüller, arXiv 2608.07578).

Faithfulness where it matters: make v4's semantics machine-checked. Run 1 built Programme.Deep (typed HOML, Henkin semantics) and shallow agreement over full and closed models (K28, K35, K40, K45, K62); build on it, do not redo it. (a) A deep proof calculus for v4's language L with soundness and completeness over L-general models (v4 Definition before prop:lgeneral). (b) v4 Proposition prop:lgeneral as a Lean theorem, the whole-term hypothesis stated for deep derivations, with a translation of at least K14's and K1's proofs into certified deep derivations. (c) Example ex:separating at all types of L (v4 formalises the propositional part only; cf. run 1 K56, K59). (d) v4's conjecture: for the variant-2 axioms, does the witness criterion alone suffice? Proof or counterexample. Read v4 main.tex lines 1890-2040 first.

Settle the open question of arXiv 2609.36279v4 ('What stays open'): is Ax1GenTwo equivalent to unrestricted Ax1Gen in variant 2 and 3' over L-general models? Done: detector-certified proofs of Two_equivalent in variants 2 and 3' (F, K135-K136), semantic Lean theorem for closed Henkin models of variant 2 over listed closure terms (K147), Ax2a+Ax4 suffice and are each needed (run 2). Remaining: the semantic theorem for variant 3', and for all L-general models rather than the listed closure terms (follows from target C (b) if that lands). State everything against the library's OpenQuestions modules.

Hybrid-free proofs certified by the author's own detector. For each L-sentence (not a frame statement like OneWorld, R_Id) in library/F_WORKLIST.md, flagged hybrid or inheriting in v4's OpenQuestions modules: either a new proof of the identical statement from the same module's definitions that passes `python /library/tools/hybrid_check.py <Module> <Full.Name>` (witness and whole-term mode), or an L-general model of the module's axioms where it fails. Start with Two_equivalent and Ax1Gen_of_Two (Ax1GenTwoVariant2, Ax1GenTwoVariant3Plain). Details and rules: library/F_WORKLIST.md.

L_R semantically. Run 3's K14 (library Programme.«20261022-1314-ontological».F.RigidHF.L_R_hf) proves L_R of OpenQuestions.Ax1GenRigidVariant2 hybrid-free, but only detector-certified. First state the rigid reading in the deep language of run 4 (v4 sec:rigid: rigid sets are given by conditions formed in L, so Ax1GenR is a schema over L-conditions; quote v4). Then prove, via a certified derivation in run 4's calculus (sound_v4_wt), that in every v4 L-general model (run 4's VM/LGen) where Ax2a, Ax2b, Ax4 hold and the Ax1GenR instance for PosGlobal = {psi | A(P psi)} holds, P G holds at every world. Match the deep axioms clause by clause to the module. Small target: one round of building, one of review.

From Lean proofs to deep derivations. Run 4's semantics (K12, K15) covers hand-written deep derivations only; the detector hole (run 4 K5, sk's HiddenNominal) shows Lean's type theory is richer than HOL. Build a Lean meta-program (tactic or command) that, for a theorem of a shallow OpenQuestions module whose proof stays in a stated fragment (HOL rules: intro/elim of the connectives and quantifiers, classical logic, Eq.subst/congrArg/congrFun, funext, propext, beta/eta, unfolding of the module's definitions), outputs a run-4 DW derivation of the deep image of its statement, kernel-checked, with the image matched by rfl; otherwise it names the first step outside the fragment or violating the whole-term condition. Must succeed on run 3's F proofs (at least TwoV2, RigidHF) and on v4's hybrid-free OpenQuestions theorems, and reject sk's HiddenNominal and congrFun probes. Prove the translation sound for the fragment if feasible.

open_questions.question: Is Ax1GenTwo equivalent to unrestricted Ax1Gen in variants 2 and 3′ without nominals?
open_questions.summary: Yes. Hybrid-free proofs of the identical statements pass the author's detector (K135, K136), and a semantic theorem covers every v4 L-general model where Ax2a, Ax2b, positivity of necessary existence and Ax4 hold (K157). Ax2a and Ax4 suffice and each is needed (K113).

open_questions.question: Can side condition (†) be dropped from the hybrid-free proof for variant 3?
open_questions.summary: Yes, semantically: in closed Henkin models of variant 3, Ax2a, Ax3, Ax4, Th4 and Ax1GenTwo give God at every world with no side condition, and this extends to all models closed under a Lean fragment of L.

open_questions.question: Rigid reading Ax1GenR: does L follow with no condition on positivity?
open_questions.summary: Yes. A detector-certified proof from Ax2a, Ax2b and Ax4 only (K146), a semantic theorem over all v4 L-general models via a certified deep derivation (K166), and a model showing Ax1GenR cannot be dropped (K167).

open_questions.question: Ax1GenBoxTwo in variant 3′: does G_ex follow hybrid-free?
open_questions.summary: Semantically, Ax1GenBoxTwo is equivalent to L under Ax2a, Ax3, Ax4 (K89), and with Ax2b added God exists at every world (K91). Without Ax2b an L-general model has a godless world (K94). No detector-certified proof yet.

open_questions.question: Ax1GenOne in variant 3: does Th4 hold hybrid-free?
open_questions.summary: Yes. Proofs of the identical statements pass the author's detector (K139), with a semantic counterpart in closed Henkin models (K90).

open_questions.question: Do hybrid-free provability and object-language validity coincide for these axioms?
open_questions.summary: A certified deep calculus is sound and complete for v4 L-general models (K159, K163). The detector, however, passes a proof of a sentence that fails in an L-general model of variant 2 (K152, K155), so detector-passing and valid differ.

open_questions.question: v4's conjecture: for the variant-2 axioms, does the witness criterion alone suffice?
open_questions.summary: No. With only the witness criterion, unrestricted Leibniz substitution derives a sentence that fails in an L-general model of variant 2 (K164). Adding the whole-term motive condition gives a calculus that is sound and complete (K162, K163).

open_questions.question: Are dropping principality and dropping rigidity distinct ways out of modal collapse?
open_questions.summary: In closed models, principality at every world plus Ax2b gives collapse; one L-general model keeps principality without Ax2b and another keeps Ax2b without principality, and both avoid collapse (K123). Current-world proper filters with A4 collapse regardless of principality (K39).
